paper_metadata.title: Nature of High-Temperature Strength of Deformed Magnesium Alloy of the Mg – Zn – Zr – REE System

evidence.quote: Results of a study of the structure, phase composition, and main parameters of high-temperature strength of forgings from deformed magnesium alloy VMD16 of the Mg – Zn – Zr – REE system in aged condition are presented.

The main role in the elevation of the high-temperature and strength properties of the alloy belongs to the thermally stable nanosize LPSO phases.
The nanosize particles of thermally stable phases, i.e., zinc zirconides and yttrium hydrides, contribute substantially into the elevation of the mechanical properties.
The steady subgrain structure detected in the alloy is preserved after the heat treatment and hardens the alloy additionally.

Analysis of the data shows that VMD16 is superior to MA12 – by 34% and by a factor of 2.3 at 150 and 200°C, respectively, for the long-term strength; – by 14% and by a factor of 1.54 at 150 and 200°C, respectively, for the creep strength.
